summary: The Planet pillar of the World Economic Forum's Stakeholder Capitalism Metrics: climate change, nature loss, fresh water availability, air and water pollution, solid waste and resource availability. It has 4 core and 12 expanded metrics.

questions.text: What was your reporting period for the GHG emissions you are reporting?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Give the start and end dates (e.g. calendar year 2024). Use the same period for all emissions figures below.

questions.text: What were your Scope 1 (direct) GHG emissions, in metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO2e)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Direct emissions from sources you own or control (e.g. fuel burnt in boilers, furnaces, company vehicles). Report in tCO2e per the GHG Protocol.

questions.text: What were your Scope 2 (purchased energy) GHG emissions, in tCO2e?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, steam, heating and cooling. Report in tCO2e per the GHG Protocol. State if location-based or market-based in the methodology question.

questions.text: Which greenhouse gases are included in your Scope 1 and Scope 2 figures?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Cover all relevant greenhouse gases as defined by the GHG Protocol. Select every gas that is included.

questions.text: What methodology or standard did you use to calculate your Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. For example the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard, emission factors used, and whether Scope 2 is location-based or market-based.

questions.text: What were your material upstream (Scope 3) GHG emissions, in tCO2e, where appropriate?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Estimate and report where appropriate: emissions from your supply chain, e.g. purchased goods and services, upstream transport, business travel, employee commuting. Report in tCO2e.

questions.text: What were your material downstream (Scope 3) GHG emissions, in tCO2e, where appropriate?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Estimate and report where appropriate: emissions from e.g. use of sold products, downstream transport, end-of-life treatment. Report in tCO2e.

questions.text: Which Scope 3 categories did you include in your Scope 3 estimate, and how did you decide they are material?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. List the GHG Protocol Scope 3 categories covered and the basis for judging them material.

questions.text: Which organisational boundary approach did you use for reporting emissions?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Adapted from GRI 305:1-3, GHG Protocol. Boundary under the GHG Protocol: how you decide which operations' emissions are counted.

questions.text: Have you fully implemented the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. The core metric asks for full implementation of the TCFD recommendations.

questions.text: If not yet fully implemented, what is your timeline (at most three years) for full TCFD implementation?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. Disclose a timeline of at most three years for full implementation, if necessary. Leave blank if already fully implemented.

questions.text: Do you disclose how your board oversees climate-related risks and opportunities (TCFD Governance)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. TCFD Governance pillar: board oversight and management's role in assessing and managing climate-related risks and opportunities.

questions.text: Do you disclose the climate-related risks and opportunities you have identified and their impact on your business, strategy and financial planning (TCFD Strategy)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. TCFD Strategy pillar, including the resilience of your strategy under different climate scenarios (including a 2°C or lower scenario).

questions.text: Do you disclose how you identify, assess and manage climate-related risks (TCFD Risk management)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. TCFD Risk Management pillar: processes for identifying, assessing and managing climate risks and integrating them into overall risk management.

questions.text: Do you disclose the metrics and targets you use to assess climate-related risks and opportunities (TCFD Metrics and targets)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. TCFD Metrics and Targets pillar, including Scope 1, 2 and 3 GHG emissions and the targets used to manage climate risks.

questions.text: Have you set, or committed to set, GHG emissions targets in line with the goals of the Paris Agreement?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. Paris goals: limit global warming to well-below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursue efforts to limit warming to 1.5°C.

questions.text: Have you set, or committed to set, a target to achieve net-zero emissions before 2050?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures, Final Report; CDSB R01, R02, R03, R04 and R06; SASB 110. Disclose whether you have set, or committed to set, a net-zero target before 2050.

disclosures.title: Nature loss: Land use and ecological sensitivity

questions.text: How many sites that you own, lease or manage are in or adjacent to protected areas?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: GRI (304-1). Count the sites owned, leased or managed in or adjacent to protected areas.

questions.text: What is the total area (in hectares) of the sites you own, lease or manage in or adjacent to protected areas?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: GRI (304-1). Report in hectares.

questions.text: How many sites that you own, lease or manage are in or adjacent to key biodiversity areas (KBA)?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: GRI (304-1). Count the sites owned, leased or managed in or adjacent to key biodiversity areas.

questions.text: What is the total area (in hectares) of the sites you own, lease or manage in or adjacent to key biodiversity areas (KBA)?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: GRI (304-1). Report in hectares.

questions.text: Can you list these sites and say where they are?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: GRI (304-1). Optional detail: site names, locations and the protected area or KBA concerned.

disclosures.title: Fresh water availability: Water consumption and withdrawal in water-stressed areas

questions.text: For your operations where it is material, how many megalitres of water did you withdraw in total?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Report in megalitres (ML).

questions.text: For your operations where it is material, how many megalitres of water did you consume in total?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Report in megalitres (ML). Consumption is water withdrawn that is not returned to the source.

questions.text: What percentage of your water withdrawal is in regions with high or extremely high baseline water stress?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Use the WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool to classify regions. Report a percentage.

questions.text: What percentage of your water consumption is in regions with high or extremely high baseline water stress?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Use the WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool to classify regions. Report a percentage.

questions.text: Where appropriate, how many megalitres of water are withdrawn across your full value chain (upstream and downstream)?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Estimate and report where appropriate, in megalitres.

questions.text: Where appropriate, how many megalitres of water are consumed across your full value chain (upstream and downstream)?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Estimate and report where appropriate, in megalitres.

questions.text: Where appropriate, what percentage of your value-chain water withdrawal and consumption is in regions with high or extremely high baseline water stress?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: SASB (CG-HP-140a.1.), WRI Aqueduct water risk atlas tool. Estimate using WRI Aqueduct. If withdrawal and consumption differ, give both percentages in the notes.

disclosures.title: Climate change: Paris-aligned GHG emissions targets

questions.text: Have you defined time-bound, science-based GHG emissions targets in line with the Paris Agreement?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Targets in line with limiting warming to well-below 2°C and pursuing 1.5°C.

questions.text: By what year before 2050 do you aim to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Enter the target year (must be before 2050).

questions.text: What interim emissions reduction targets have you set (reduction amount and target year)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Interim targets based on Science Based Targets initiative methodologies, if applicable.

questions.text: Are your targets validated by the Science Based Targets initiative?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Select the status of your SBTi validation.

questions.text: What progress have you made against your targets so far?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Report progress against each target, e.g. percentage reduction achieved vs the base year.

questions.text: If you take an alternative approach to setting targets, what methodology did you use to calculate them?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Answer only if you do not use the Science Based Targets initiative methodology.

questions.text: If you take an alternative approach, on what basis do your targets deliver the goals of the Paris Agreement?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: Science-Based Targets initiative. Answer only if an alternative approach is taken.

disclosures.title: Climate change: Impact of greenhouse gas emissions

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact (monetary value) of your Scope 1 GHG emissions, where material?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: US EPA fact sheet on the Social Cost of Carbon (2016); Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Value your Scope 1 emissions using a social cost of carbon. Report the amount and currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your Scope 2 GHG emissions, where material?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: US EPA fact sheet on the Social Cost of Carbon (2016); Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Value your Scope 2 emissions using a social cost of carbon.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your Scope 3 GHG emissions along the value chain, where material?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: US EPA fact sheet on the Social Cost of Carbon (2016); Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Value your material Scope 3 emissions using a social cost of carbon.

questions.text: What estimate of the social cost of carbon did you use (per tonne of CO2e)?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: US EPA fact sheet on the Social Cost of Carbon (2016); Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. State the value used per tCO2e and its currency/year in notes.

questions.text: What is the source or basis of the social cost of carbon estimate you used?
questions.hint: Climate change · Source: US EPA fact sheet on the Social Cost of Carbon (2016); Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. For example the US EPA social cost of carbon, ISO 14008, Natural Capital Protocol or Value Balancing Alliance.

disclosures.title: Nature loss: Land use and ecological sensitivity

questions.text: What area of land (in hectares) do your own operations use to produce basic plant, animal or mineral commodities?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. For example land used for forestry, agriculture or mining. Report if applicable.

questions.text: What area of land (in hectares) is used to produce the basic commodities in your full supply chain, where material?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. Supply-chain figures can initially be estimated from the mass of each commodity used and the average mass produced per unit of land in each sourcing location.

questions.text: What is the year-on-year change in the area of land used for your operations?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. Report change versus the previous year (in hectares or percent, state in notes).

questions.text: What is the year-on-year change in the area of land used in your supply chain?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. Report change versus the previous year, estimated if necessary.

questions.text: What percentage of this land area, or of your commodity inputs by mass or cost, is covered by a sustainability certification standard or sustainable management programme?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. State the basis (land area, mass or cost) in notes.

questions.text: Which certification standards or sustainable management programmes cover it?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. Name each standard or programme, or describe it.

questions.text: What percentage of total land area, mass or cost is covered by each standard or programme?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: New metric. List each standard/programme with its percentage.

disclosures.title: Nature loss: Impact of land use and conversion

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact (monetary value) of your use of land, where material?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your conversion of ecosystems, where material?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What valuation methodology did you use to value land use and conversion impacts?
questions.hint: Nature loss · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. E.g. Natural Capital Protocol, ISO 14008, Value Balancing Alliance.

disclosures.title: Fresh water availability: Impact of freshwater consumption and withdrawal

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact (monetary value) of your freshwater withdrawal, where material?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your freshwater consumption, where material?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What valuation methodology did you use to value freshwater impacts?
questions.hint: Fresh water availability · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. E.g. Natural Capital Protocol, ISO 14008, Value Balancing Alliance.

questions.text: What were your nitrogen oxides (NOx) emissions, in metric tonnes, along the value chain where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: GRI 305-7. Report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: What were your sulphur oxides (SOx) emissions, in metric tonnes, along the value chain where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: GRI 305-7. Report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: What were your particulate matter emissions, in metric tonnes, along the value chain where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: GRI 305-7. Report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: What other significant air emissions do you have, and in what quantities?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: GRI 305-7. E.g. volatile organic compounds, hazardous air pollutants; give quantities and units.

questions.text: What proportion of these emissions occurs in or adjacent to urban or densely populated areas?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: GRI 305-7. Estimate as a percentage wherever possible.

disclosures.title: Air pollution: Impact of air pollution

questions.text: What is the valued impact of your NOx and SOx emissions, where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued impact of your particulate matter emissions, where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued impact of your other significant air emissions, where material?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What valuation methodology did you use to value air pollution impacts?
questions.hint: Air pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. E.g. Natural Capital Protocol, ISO 14008, Value Balancing Alliance.

questions.text: How many metric tonnes of nitrogen in fertilizer did you consume, where material along the value chain?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: SASB (CN0101-11). Estimate and report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: How many metric tonnes of phosphate in fertilizer did you consume, where material along the value chain?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: SASB (CN0101-11). Estimate and report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: How many metric tonnes of potassium in fertilizer did you consume, where material along the value chain?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: SASB (CN0101-11). Estimate and report wherever material along the value chain.

questions.text: How did you estimate your fertilizer consumption, and which parts of the value chain are covered?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: SASB (CN0101-11). Describe the method and boundary (own operations, suppliers).

disclosures.title: Water pollution: Impact of water pollution

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of excess nutrients you release to water, where material?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of heavy metals you release to water, where material?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of other toxins you release to water, where material?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What valuation methodology did you use to value water pollution impacts?
questions.hint: Water pollution · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. E.g. Natural Capital Protocol, ISO 14008, Value Balancing Alliance.

questions.text: How many metric tonnes of single-use plastic did you consume across your full value chain?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: New metric. Report an estimate in metric tonnes.

questions.text: What are the most significant applications of single-use plastic you identified?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: New metric. E.g. packaging, cutlery, bags.

questions.text: What quantification approach did you use to estimate single-use plastic?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: New metric. Describe how the tonnage was estimated.

questions.text: How do you define "single-use plastic"?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: New metric. State the definition you adopted.

disclosures.title: Solid waste: Impact of solid waste disposal

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your plastic waste disposal, where material?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What is the valued societal impact of your other solid waste streams disposed of, where material?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. Report along the value chain wherever material; state currency in notes.

questions.text: What valuation methodology did you use to value solid waste disposal impacts?
questions.hint: Solid waste · Source: Natural Capital Protocol (2016); ISO 14008 (2019); Value Balancing Alliance. E.g. Natural Capital Protocol, ISO 14008, Value Balancing Alliance.

questions.text: Do you report a resource circularity metric?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Report the most appropriate metric(s) for the company and/or a product, material or site.

questions.text: At what level do you measure circularity?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Select all that apply.

questions.text: Which circularity metric(s) do you use?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Examples: Circular Transition Indicators (WBCSD & KPMG), Ellen MacArthur Foundation Circulytics, or a company-developed metric.

questions.text: What are the results of your chosen circularity metric(s)?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Report the value(s) with units and the scope they apply to.

questions.text: What methodological approach did you use to calculate the chosen metric(s)?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Describe the calculation approach.

questions.text: What is the rationale for choosing these metric(s)?
questions.hint: Resource availability · Source: WBCSD & KPMG "Circular Transition Indicators"; Ellen MacArthur Foundation "Circulytics™ indicators". Explain why they are most appropriate for you.
